synthesis: Scout users authenticate via email+password through a one-shot onboarding flow: admin grants `clarity-scout` permission + assigns kit → user receives signed URL email (7-day TTL) → sets password via `/scout/set-password/{user}` → can login via `/api/scout/login`. The signed URL cannot be reused once `email_verified_at` is set (ScoutSetPasswordController:71-73). If a user forgets their email OR password after onboarding, they have NO recovery path—neither self-serve nor admin-assisted. Clarity's admin/client panels use passwordless OTP (OneTimePassword:32-50 sends 6-digit code, cached for `password_timeout` seconds). The ticket requests adding Scout account recovery, preferring OTP/magic-link (Clarity-consistent) with an admin-assist backstop so users are never permanently locked out.

questions.text: Should we REPLACE password auth entirely with OTP-only (Clarity-consistent, simpler UX) or SUPPORT BOTH (smoother migration, no forced re-onboard)? Replacing is cleaner long-term but requires all existing Scout users to switch to OTP; supporting both adds complexity (two auth paths) but avoids breaking existing logins.

When admin resends onboarding link, should it ALWAYS work (override `email_verified_at` guard) or only for unverified users? The current guard (ScoutSetPasswordController:71-73) rejects verified users to prevent link reuse, but admin-initiated resend is intentional recovery, not a security bypass.

Should Scout OTP use the SAME cache key/TTL as Clarity admin (`otp_{email}`, `password_timeout` seconds) or a separate Scout-specific key/TTL? Same key = simpler, but if a user is both a Scout driver and an admin, one OTP request would invalidate the other.

notes.auth_architecture: Clarity has TWO auth surfaces: (1) Filament admin+client panels use passwordless OTP (CustomLoginPage, OneTimePassword class), (2) Scout PWA uses Sanctum bearer tokens from email+password login (ClarityScoutAuthController). The PWA is a separate Vue SPA served at `/scout/{any?}` with its own `/api/scout/login` endpoint (routes/api.php:104-125 in current main). Ticket wants Scout to match Clarity's OTP flow.
notes.onboarding_flow: Admin grants `clarity-scout` permission via ScoutUserProvisioner (app/Support/Scout/ScoutUserProvisioner.php:84-143), which sends ScoutOnboardingNotification (app/Notifications/ScoutOnboardingNotification.php:24-45) with a 7-day signed URL to `/scout/set-password/{user}`. User sets password, `email_verified_at` is set (ScoutSetPasswordController.php:39-41), and the link becomes one-shot (line 71: `if ($user->hasVerifiedEmail()) rejectWith('used')`). After that, user can login via password at `/api/scout/login` (ClarityScoutAuthController.php:21-87).
notes.precedent_onboarding_signed_url: prior onboarding signed-URL work fixed 'Scout onboarding set-password signed URL 403 Invalid signature'—ValidateScoutSignedUrl (app/Http/Middleware/ValidateScoutSignedUrl.php) now accepts both absolute and relative signed URLs (line 22: `hasValidSignature(absolute: true) || hasValidSignature(absolute: false)`), and shows a friendly error page instead of bare 403. This means signed URL infrastructure is solid; the gap is post-onboarding recovery.
notes.precedent_force_login_org_scoping: prior force-login org-scoping work fixed 'Scout force-login minted unscoped token'—admin impersonation via ClarityScoutForceLoginController must stay org-scoped. Any admin password-reset action must NOT regress this; ensure the reset path respects org boundaries (user must belong to acting admin's org or admin must be InsightLPR staff).
notes.clarity_otp_details: OneTimePassword class (app/Filament/Auth/OneTimePassword.php): sends 6-digit code via OneTimePasswordNotification, stores in cache as `otp_{email}` for `password_timeout` seconds (config/auth.php, default 900s = 15min). CustomLoginPage (app/Filament/Auth/CustomLoginPage.php): bypasses OTP in non-prod (lines 73-83), sends OTP on first submit (lines 84-87), verifies on second submit (lines 89-106). Scout would replicate this flow but use Sanctum token response instead of web session.
